overview.text: The Horseshoe Whip Snake is a long, slender, harmless snake of south-western Europe and north-western Africa, named after the horseshoe-shaped mark on its head.

identification.text: Slender with a head wider than the neck, large eyes with round pupils and a row of small scales under each eye; a series of large dark spots runs down the back.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Up to about 1.5 to 1.8 m; males and females are the same size.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Portugal, southern, central and eastern Spain, Gibraltar, southern Sardinia and Pantelleria, and Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.

distribution.label: Introduced
distribution.text: Since the early 2000s on Mallorca, Ibiza and Formentera (Balearic Islands), probably arriving with olive trees imported from mainland Spain.

habitat.text: Mediterranean scrub, rocky places and shores, farmland, pasture, plantations, gardens and towns.

reproduction.text: Lays eggs in early summer, which hatch in late summer; one study found about 6.8 eggs per clutch on average.

recognise.text: Large dark spots down a slender body.
Row of small scales under the eye.
